title: fix(runtime)!: the dispatcher's PATCH /data/:object/:id honours a body expectedVersion and If-Match, as RestServer's twin does
body:
Fixes #23462
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

The runtime dispatcher's `PATCH /data/:object/:id` now reads the optimistic-concurrency token the way `RestServer`'s twin reads it, strips it from the patch, and forwards it to `updateData`. A stale update through the dispatcher is refused instead of applied, and a body `expectedVersion` is no longer handed to the engine as a field. This is the `PATCH` position of the family whose `DELETE` position landed as PR #23460 (`3d231ba787`), and it mirrors that landing's shapes.

Dispatched by the `domain:cli` seat 2 PM (claim `6167715147`, branch `claude/issue-23462-dispatcher-patch-version`), session `session_01Q9PZ5Pzqcus4woVvTZwWNU`.

## What was wrong

`RestServer` (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:9014-9063`, read only) does three things:
- it reads the body's `expectedVersion`, else `If-Match`;
- it strips `expectedVersion` out of the patch, whatever its value;
- it hands `String(token)` to `updateData` when the token is truthy.

The protocol then refuses an update whose record has moved (`409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE`). The dispatcher dropped the token twice:

1. `domains/data.ts`, the `PATCH` branch, read neither and passed the whole body as `data`.
2. `action-execution.ts`, `callData`'s update arm, forwarded only `{ object, id, data }` to `updateData`.

Measured before the fix (the pin file on unfixed source, `94f0cf085e`), through `dispatch()`:
- A stale `If-Match` answered `200` and wrote the row.
- A body `expectedVersion` was refused `400 INVALID_FIELD` ("Unknown field 'expectedVersion' on object 'task'"). The `createHonoApp` catch-all renders that as the `500` the card measured.

## What changes

- **`domains/data.ts`, the `PATCH` branch.**
  - Reads the body's `expectedVersion` (when the body is an object), else `If-Match`, through the private `requestIfMatch` reader PR #23460 added. There is no second spelling of it.
  - Strips the key from the patch when present, whatever its value.
  - Forwards `String(token)` only when the token is truthy.
  - These are REST's own statements, so both doors send `updateData` the same request.
- **`action-execution.ts`, `callData`'s update arm.** Forwards `params.expectedVersion` to `updateData` when present. Every other caller (`mcp.ts`, the declarative update action, the endpoint executor) sends `{ object, id, data }` and reaches `updateData` as before.
- **The ObjectQL fallback.** A token sent to a host whose protocol has no `updateData` is refused `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` before anything is read or written, in the delete arm's shape. An update with no token reaches the fallback as before.
- **The changeset**, `.changeset/23462-dispatcher-patch-expected-version.md`, follows PR #23460's shape:
  - `@objectstack/runtime` `minor`, `fix(runtime)!:`, FROM → TO;
  - one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`;
  - the launch-window BREAKING line.

  It says a `createHonoApp` host still renders the refusal as `500` with the record unchanged. It promises no wire `409` there.

## Pins

The new file `packages/runtime/src/domains/data-update-expected-version.test.ts` is the `PATCH` sibling of `data-delete-expected-version.test.ts`, on the same rig:
- a real better-sqlite3 store, the real `ObjectQL` engine and a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`;
- `RestServer`'s registered handler and `HttpDispatcher.dispatch()` side by side. The dispatch side repeats the catch-all's statements over a real Fetch `Request`, with the body parsed from a clone of its text.

Every row reads the store after the request.

- **Per door, 5 rows each:**
  - no token updates, and `updateData` receives no token;
  - the current body token updates, and the patch handed over carries no `expectedVersion` key;
  - a stale body token is refused `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE`, and the row is unchanged;
  - `If-Match` behaves like the body token, both current and stale;
  - the body token is judged before `If-Match`.
- **Side by side, 6 token shapes plus the Node header record.** The shapes are: a stale token; a number token; `null` beside a stale `If-Match`; `null` beside the current one; `''` beside a stale `If-Match`; a body that is only the current token. For each, the two doors must agree on status, code and the row, and the key never reaches the engine as a field.
- **The fallback, 3 rows.** A body token and `If-Match` each get `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, with neither `find` nor `update` called. An unguarded update still reaches the fallback.

How a refusal is read: as on `DELETE`, `/data` has no local catch. So the conflict is the protocol's `ConcurrentUpdateError`, thrown out of `dispatch()`. It is read through `resolveThrownHttpError` (`@objectstack/types`) and set beside what `RestServer` answered through `mapDataError`.

**Before and after.**
- **Before** (unfixed source, `94f0cf085e`): `Tests 13 failed | 7 passed (20)`. Every `RestServer` row and both controls were green. Every catch-all token row and both `501` rows were red.
- **After** (`19d1b8dfdd`), run with the landed `DELETE` file: `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 40 passed (40)`.

**Ablations.** Each ran through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, with a restore trap in the driver.
- Each anchor hit once, and `mutation landed` was printed.
- Each restore was proven by the blob hash equalling HEAD's and an empty `git diff HEAD`.
- The expected direction was red each time, and each went red.
- The pins import `../http-dispatcher.js` relatively, so the mutated source is what ran, and no `dist` was involved.

The four readings:
- **A**, the `data.ts` forward dropped: `10 failed | 10 passed`.
  - Red: the catch-all token rows; the side-by-side stale, number and null-beside-stale rows; the header-record row; both `501` rows, because no token reaches `callData`.
  - Green: every `RestServer` row, both controls, and the three side-by-side rows that do not depend on the forward.
  - A first attempt was refused by the tool itself before anything ran: the replacement `data,` was a prefix of the anchor, so its count could not rise. It measured nothing, and it was redone with a marker comment.
- **B**, the `callData` update-arm forward dropped: `8 failed | 12 passed`. The same token rows went red. Both `501` rows stayed green, because the refusal is its own statement.
- **C**, the fallback refusal disabled (`if (false)`): `2 failed | 18 passed`, the two `501` rows.
- **D**, the strip dropped: `9 failed | 11 passed`. This one goes beyond the dispatch's three, for the card's "a body token is never written as a field". Every body-token row went red, and the `If-Match`-only rows stayed green.

## Mechanism readings (the dispatch's hypotheses)

- **(a) Confirmed.** REST's twin is at `rest-server.ts:9014-9063`, as described. It is mirrored, and no `@objectstack/rest` export is added.
- **(b) Confirmed.** `requestIfMatch` is reused, and so are the delete arm's forward and its `501` shape. There is no second spelling of the reader.
- **(c) Measured on both doors**, in a scratch rig that is not committed.
  - On every token shape, the doors now agree:
    - a number or object token is stringified and judged (`409` when stale);
    - `null` falls through to `If-Match`;
    - `false` or `''` is stripped and forwarded as no token, so `If-Match` is not read (REST's `??`, then its truthy test);
    - the quoted-empty `""` is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` by the protocol, on both doors.
  - On a body that is NOT a record, the doors still differ, and not about the token:
    - `RestServer`'s `UpdateDataRequestSchema` gate answers `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` for an array, string or number body, and `200` for `null` (patched as `{}`);
    - the dispatcher answers `500` (the engine's own error), with nothing written.
  - That divergence predates this change: the dispatcher never had REST's body-schema gate. It is a different defect class from this card, so it is reported as a finding, not fixed here.
- **(d) Confirmed.**
  - Through `dispatch()`, a stale update throws `ConcurrentUpdateError`, read as `409 / CONCURRENT_UPDATE`.
  - Through a real `createHonoApp`, a stale body token and a stale `If-Match` each answer `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` with the conflict sentence, and the row is unchanged. The current token and no token answer `200` and update. This was a scratch run, not committed: the adapter source over the runtime `dist` built at `19d1b8dfdd`.
  - The `500` comes from the catch-all rendering from `statusCode` alone. #23365 remains open for it, and nothing there is edited here.
- **(e) No `hono-*` pin added, so no surface supplement is needed.**
  - The two hand-offs a `PATCH` token rides are already pinned at the adapter:
    - `hono.test.ts` ("PATCH /api/data/account parses JSON body") pins that the parsed body reaches `dispatch()`;
    - `hono-catch-all-raw-request.test.ts` pins the raw `Request`, where `If-Match` rides, for `PUT`/`PATCH`.
  - The domain's reading of both is pinned here, through `dispatch()`.
  - The one fact a composed-host pin would add is the wire status, which today is #23365's `500`. Pinning it would pin that defect.
  - The end-to-end reading above was taken instead, as PR #23460 did.

## Gates (final head `75d46f1034`)

This head merges `origin/main` at `1baf976cf9` (#23458, #23466, #23464). The incoming commits touched nothing on this path. They touched:
- `metadata-protocol`'s `dropStorage` delete;
- the Hono adapter's repeated-query handling;
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` and `sandbox/*`;
- `packages/spec` (the hook schema).

After the merge: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `rm -rf packages/runtime/.objectstack`, and the runtime closure rebuilt (`pnpm --filter '@objectstack/runtime...' build`, VERDICT exit 0).

- **Typecheck.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime run typecheck` exits 0. That covers `tsc --noEmit` and `check:test-typecheck`: 27 files, 190 errors, 68 pinned signatures held. The new test is compiled by `tsconfig.test.json` (`--listFilesOnly`: 1 hit) and excluded from `tsconfig.json` (0 hits).
- **Tests.** `vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2` on `@objectstack/runtime`: `Test Files 377 passed (377)`, `Tests 5507 passed | 19 skipped (5526)`.
- **Derived gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` gives 65 commands. All ran at this head, each exit code captured before any pipe:
  - 64 exit 0;
  - `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 3, `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, because it reads a whole-repo `pnpm build`. It is NOT MEASURED locally, and CI runs it.

  The `--ran` reconciliation reads `65 derived, 64 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED (derived from a recorded exit 3), 0 UNRUN`.
- **Roster gates.** The five whose roster sits under a touched directory also ran, each exit 0: `check-changeset-fixed`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check:route-ledger-census`.
- **`pnpm lint`, as a declared narrowing.** The evidence:
  1. The diff touches no eslint config or ignore file.
  2. `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config`, with the repo config, over the three changed source files exits 0 with empty output.
  3. The config is untyped and per-file. `eslint.config.mjs` says it "never enables type-aware linting", and `data.ts` has 6 active rules, none cross-file. So no unchanged file's verdict can move with this diff.

  CI runs the full `eslint .`.

## Acceptance notes

Observations, not filed:
- A `?expectedVersion` query on a `PATCH` is read by neither door: both apply a stale update sent that way. The spec declares the `PATCH` token as the body field or `If-Match`, so this is an undeclared spelling.
- The declared-endpoint door (`endpoint-executor.ts`, `object_operation: update`) also hands `ctx.body` over as `data` and reads no token. This is a read-only inference, not measured.

Two findings are handed to the seat for filing, in the `os-dev-report` comment on #23462:
- the non-record body divergence described under (c);
- an empty or `false` body token that silences a stale `If-Match`, on both doors.
